text.p: Following are highlights of the main stories in Croatian dailies on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
VJESNIK
- The Tudjman-Izetbegovic meeting is most probably not going to be held during July due to the tight schedule of Croatian and Bosnian presidents, a commentary says.
- UNTAES military contingent starts its withdrawal from Serb-populated region of Eastern Slavonia.
- Washington Times publishes four pages of articles dedicated to Croatia.
- Croatia to build some 27 exits at the Bajakovo border crossing into the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, as this crossing is expcted to be the busiest of all.
- The members of the pensioners' association send a note to president Tudjman asking him to secure them a better life, in line with the promises he made in the state of the nation address.
- The deputy Finance Minister Mijo Jukic announces that all the bogus insurance companies will be dealt with accordingly.
- Shipper Croatia Line to receive a $99 million syndicated loan.
VECERNJI LIST
- The Zagreb Stock Exchange waives its regular fee between July 14 and August 14 in a bid to push more trading in the lean summer period.
- A new legislation on Zagreb's communal law and order which is to come into effect in three weeks' time will have the citizens paying 100 kuna fines for every piece of paper they drop in the street.
- Grey economy is going to be defeated by modern technology, reseacarcher at the Institute for Public Finances Predral Bajakovic says in an interview.
SLOBODNA DALMACIJA
- Private accommodation facilities along the Adriatic are becoming packed as part of the 1997 tourism revival.
- Value added tax, to be applied from next year with a rate of 22 percent, will push prices up by 2.3 to 5.2 percent and cause an inflation of 1.7 percent, according to Institute for Public Finances.
- Eastern Slavonia will become part of the Croatian power grid by August 15.

- "Our first goal is to increase output in two plants. We also plan to replace crude oil with coal as the main fuel," says Friedrich Fercho of the Readymix Corporation, which recently became majority owner of cementworks Dalmacijacement.
- There were 267,746 jobless in June, 2.5 percent less than in May, but up 6.0 percent from June last year.

- Croatia's 1996 GDP increase of 4.2 percent from 1995 shows improvement of economic growth, but it is still way below pre-war levels and equals only 74.15 percent of GDP in 1990. -- Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075
